craft_notes: Sthāyin: sovereign-speech (self-yoked one IS Bhairava: his speech does deeds — curser-and-favorer: the vīra undertow lands). Rows: row 3 (becomes→making). Close: making (the deed-word: speech that MAKES curse-and-favor: śāpānugraha as one compound act). Rejected: 'blessings and curses' split — killed: curse-and-favor kept (order kept: curse FIRST, the fierce priority); 'becomes Bhairava' softened — killed: himself-becomes kept (svayam as the sovereignty-word: no becoming-by-other).

lines: Here and in one yoked — Bhairava himself becomes:
by speech deeds does — curse-and-favor making.
l4.sanskrit_cite: atra caikatame yukto jāyate bhairavaḥ svayam | vācā karoti karmāṇi śāpānugrahakārakaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What happens in one's own yoking? → Self-yoked, one IS Bhairava — his speech becomes curser-and-favorer.
c1_essence: Yoked here: IS Bhairava; speech curser-and-favorer.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vīra undertow (stillness that ends in sovereignty)
